q: Kahn's algorithm starts with which nodes?
options: The node with the most edges
why: They have no prerequisites left, so they can go first.

q: How does Kahn's algorithm detect a cycle?
options: Fewer than V nodes end up in the order
why: Nodes on a cycle wait on each other and never reach in-degree 0.

q: Course Schedule gives [a, b] meaning "to take a you must first take b". Which edge?
why: Edges point from prerequisite to the course that needs it.
Each node is queued once and each edge decremented once.

q: Is the topological order of a DAG unique?
options: Not in general; many valid orders can exist
why: Any order respecting all edges is valid.

q: You need to detect a cycle in an UNDIRECTED graph. Is Kahn's algorithm the right tool?
options: No: in-degrees are for directed graphs; use union-find or DFS with a parent check
why: Undirected edges have no direction for in-degrees to measure.
